primary_claim: Using steering-vector-generated honest alternatives alongside original responses (JUSSA) raises LLM-judge sycophancy detection accuracy from 42% (single response) to 77%, versus an 89% paired-evaluation gold standard.
stated_future_work: Investigating whether models exhibit "internalized manipulation"—deceptive behavior that emerges without explicit prompting, embedded within learned patterns
limitations_stated: Datasets were tailored to Gemma-2-2B-it; other models might respond differently to manipulation-provoking prompts or refuse entirely
Llama-7b-chat shows excessive sycophancy on provoked prompts, making detection easier for Single Judge in that case
Effectiveness depends on having good honesty-promoting steering vectors; more work needed on which behaviors generalize
A few categories (False Dichotomy, False Credentials, False Causality) showed variable validation results
Realistic cases of internalized subtle manipulation are very hard to find
quote: Single response evaluation: Judges correctly identified sycophancy only 42% of the time; JUSSA evaluation: Judges correctly identified sycophancy 77% of the time; Paired evaluation (gold standard): 89% accuracy
